findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` without arguments, but the only method defined in the superclass UsernamePasswordForm is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. There is no no-arg overload, so this does not compile. Either add a no-arg variant (e.g. `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`) or pass `context.getUser()`.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires a non-null user, disabling conditional passkeys on normal (first) login
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`. It is used in authenticate() (line 115) and challenge() (line 137) to decide whether to call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)`. Previously the form was filled when the user was NOT yet identified (`context.getUser() == null`), which is exactly the conditional-UI/passkey autofill case for a fresh login. With this change, a regular login (no user in the context) no longer gets the WebAuthn conditional-UI attributes, so passkey autofill/login from the username+password page is broken for the primary use case, while it is only enabled during re-authentication. The user!=null condition appears inverted / should not gate passkey setup at all.
